title: Local CEN/CENELEC JTC 21 engineering reference cache for EU AI Act Annex IV
scope: Deterministic technical-document lookup for Articles 12, 14, and 15. Inclusion does not establish legal conformity, harmonisation, or admissibility.
constitutional_rule: Not a conformity assessment. Counsel classifies.

standards.title: Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Management system

evidence_requirements.description: Document logging ownership, retention controls, event taxonomy, and evidence-retrieval procedures for the deployed system.
Map management-system responsibilities, competence records, operating controls, and human-oversight procedures to the deployed system.
Map security-governance ownership, risk controls, and incident-management processes to the deployed system.

limitations: This fixture is an engineering reference and does not claim that the designation was harmonised for the EU AI Act at the review date.
Management-system evidence supports but does not by itself establish technical conformity.
Counsel must verify the current Official Journal and Commission designation status before reliance.

standards.title: Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Guidance on risk management

evidence_requirements.description: Document how identified risks are controlled through human-oversight measures, including intervention criteria and residual-risk escalation.
Map risk-treatment decisions, monitoring signals, and incident-response responsibilities to the deployed AI system.

limitations: The record is a technical risk-management reference and is not represented as delegated-act harmonised.
A risk-management process does not by itself prove accuracy, robustness, or cybersecurity.
The deployment owner must document system-specific risk decisions and acceptance authority.

standards.title: Information security, cybersecurity and privacy protection — Information security management systems — Requirements

evidence_requirements.description: Document protected audit logging, logging responsibility, retention, integrity protection, and review of security-relevant events.
Map information-security controls, access restrictions, threat handling, and incident-management evidence to the deployed system.

limitations: This engineering reference is not represented as harmonised under the EU AI Act at the review date.
Certification or management-system evidence does not itself establish Article 15 conformity of an AI system.
Prompt-injection controls require deployment-specific validation and must not be inferred solely from the management-system record.

standards.title: Information security, cybersecurity and privacy protection — Information security controls

evidence_requirements.description: Select and document event-logging, logging-monitoring, retention, and protection controls appropriate to the deployed system.
Document secure-development, access-control, threat-handling, and incident-management controls with deployment-specific test evidence.

limitations: The catalogue entry is a technical control catalogue and is not represented as EU AI Act harmonisation.
The standard provides guidance rather than deployment-specific proof of robustness or cybersecurity.
Control selection and validation remain the responsibility of the deployer and relevant assurance personnel.

standards.title: Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Artificial intelligence concepts and terminology

evidence_requirements.description: Use consistent terminology when documenting the system, intended purpose, operating context, event concepts, and evidence boundaries.
Describe human-oversight concepts, responsibilities, intervention mechanisms, and system limitations without implying legal conformity from terminology alone.
Use consistent terminology for robustness, cybersecurity, and related system properties in the technical documentation.

limitations: Terminology standards support consistent documentation but do not provide conformity-assessment methods or deployment evidence.
This record is not represented as harmonised under the EU AI Act at the review date.
Definitions must not be used to replace control implementation, testing, or legal classification.

standards.title: Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Framework for AI system engineering

evidence_requirements.description: Document how lifecycle, operational, monitoring, and incident events are generated, correlated, retained, and made available as evidence.
Map operational design domain, human-oversight functions, monitoring, intervention, and feedback controls into the system lifecycle.
Document engineering controls and test evidence for robustness, cybersecurity, data governance, and secure operation.

limitations: The framework supports system-engineering documentation but does not itself establish legal conformity.
This catalogue record is not represented as a delegated act harmonising the cited designation for the EU AI Act.
Deployment-specific architecture, validation results, and acceptance decisions must be retained as separate evidence.
